title: Touring with Walter Barnes and bands around Natchez
summary: Punch recounts three years with Walter Barnes, who died in the fire after Punch left, and Bud Scott and Joe Gabriel's string bands.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah. Now they used to have a nice road, they used to come when they had the old basin, that Howard Avenue, Ramport, they used to come up there and come up in the boat, in the boat, you know. Come right to Ramport and Chewie and Howard Avenue in that big, what do you call it, a pond or a river or something there, and they'd get off there and get on the float, and go on down Ramport to Connelly. But after they closed that up, that killed their route, see. I want to ask you, did you ever play around Natchez much? I went to Natchez and played with this boy who got burned up, Walter Barnes. Played there for two, three years with him, and how lucky I was. Well he was the father there, see how he'd do, he'd go out in the winter, see he'd got a big grocery store in Chicago. Well every winter he'd make up a band and make it around, see. But when he'd get back to town, the band's gone, he'd get some groceries, see. He'd think about the band that summer. And he had a big old bus, you know, and hauled people everywhere, all over the country in that bus. Well, for that reason he would have a different band every year in your bus. He'd say, you know, you just didn't have anything to go back with him. Well this year, when he got burned up, I was waiting at a place called South Chicago, see, in a club. And I told him I couldn't make the trip, because I had a nice job. And sure enough, they went out and got burned up. But I had been with him about three years.
And he had a grocery store in Chicago. Yeah, a big grocery store.

On Prairie Street. Prairie and 50 Fights I believe it was. Something like that. Did you know Bud Scott and that business? Yeah, I know them before I went to Chicago. Used to come down to my home, play music with the white folks, you know. What kind of a band did he have? Bass, guitar, and guitar. Yeah, I know them before I went to Chicago. I think he used to carry two violins. Bass, guitar, guitar, trumpet, but the guy had to play with a mule all night, you know. Soft music. What do you name too? Joe Gabriel, you heard of him? Yeah. They had the same kind of band. They had the same kind of band. They used to come down to my home, play music with the white folks, you know. What kind of a band did he have? Well, one of them, saw, he had a lot of strings, you know. I think he used to carry two violins, bass, guitar, trumpet, but the guy had to play with a mule all night, you know. Soft music. I was with him. They had the same kind of band. Same kind of band.
Would the trumpet player play by ear or would he read?
Well, I believe they'd read music, yeah. I believe that. Straight band. Yeah. Used to play some sweet soft music though boy. Like a whistler, you know.
Who else did you know in Natchez?
You didn't actually spend much time in Natchez?

Oh, we'd play a dance like Natchez and get on the bus and ride. Our best out was Florida, see. We hit spots that we'd get in Florida, see. That's where he made his money, in Florida. Every time he went to Florida, he cleaned up.
